sources.title: SpaceX loses bid to toss NAACP lawsuit over Memphis data center air pollution
sources.text:
SpaceX's AI division, SpaceXAI, lost its bid to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit, which is proceeding in federal court in Mississippi, according to a judge's opinion released late Friday.
The lawsuit claims that the AI division of CEO Elon Musk's aerospace and defense tech conglomerate violated the Clean Air Act with its use of gas-fired combustion turbines to power its massive AI data centers in Greater Memphis.
The Colossus data centers and a power plant that SpaceXAI is also building in Southaven, Mississippi, have faced community backlash for years.
The Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice filed the suit on behalf of the NAACP in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi in April 2026.
The suit alleges that between August and December 2025, xAI and its subsidiary MZX Tech, installed and operated 27 gas turbines in Southaven, Mississippi, "without an air permit or regard for the health and safety of people living nearby."
(SpaceXAI is owned and operated by SpaceX, which has rebranded it as SpaceXAI or SpaceXSI.)
The turbines emit smog-forming pollutants and particulate matter that can increase health risks and cause an unpleasant odor, among other unwanted impacts, according to the suit.
Lawyers for SpaceXAI argued in their motion to dismiss, filed in June, that the NAACP suit should be tossed because the company's use of the turbines, which it characterized as "mobile," was exempt from permitting requirements. They also argued that NAACP didn't have a right to sue under the federal Clean Air Act, and suits by such community groups were unconstitutional.
The judge presiding over the case rejected those arguments, writing: "Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not 'mobile sources' under Mississippi's SIP, and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs' claims will proceed."
The decision comes about two weeks after the same court rejected a Department of Justice's request to end the case against Musk's company.
SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

sources.title: Judge allows NAACP lawsuit over xAI data center pollution to move forward
sources.text:
A federal judge denied a motion by xAI seeking to dismiss an NAACP lawsuit accusing the SpaceX-owned company of failing to obtain permits needed to operate the gas turbines powering its Colossus data center outside Memphis.
Suing on behalf of the NAACP, the Southern Environmental Law Center said the AI company had “installed and operated at least 35 combustion turbines and other sources of air pollution at the Colossus site without ever obtaining the necessary preconstruction or operating air permits.” It also accused xAI of violating the Clean Air Act.
xAI sought to have the lawsuit dismissed, claiming that the turbines are exempt from permitting requirements because they’re mobile. The company also argued that the plaintiffs did not have the standing to sue.
“Because the plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, because the combustion turbines are not ‘mobile sources’ under Mississippi’s [State Implementation Plan], and because the citizen suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the private nondelegation doctrine, the plaintiffs’ claims will proceed,” Judge Debra M. Brown wrote in her decision.
Focusing on xAI’s claim that these kinds of citizen lawsuits are unconstitutional, Judge Brown wrote, “Because citizen suit plaintiffs sue on their own behalf, in their own name, and seek penalties that redress harm to themselves, they are not exercising the federal government’s executive power.”
TechCrunch has reached out to SpaceX for comment.
In a statement, the NAACP’s director of environmental and climate justice Abre’ Connor described this as “another important victory in our effort to hold xAI accountable.” (A similar motion to dismiss from the Department of Justice was denied earlier this month)
“The courts have repeatedly rejected attempts by xAI and the DOJ to dismiss the NAACP’s Clean Air Act case, affirming our right to pursue justice for communities impacted by pollution,” Connor said. “Our position has been clear: xAI cannot operate gas turbines without the required permits.”
The NAACP lawsuit is moving forward as public opinion seems to have turned sharply against data centers, with New York recently passing a moratorium on new data centers and other state and local governments considering similar measures.
The backlash also prompted Amazon and Microsoft to promise to stop using NDAs in their dealings with government agencies, and it could be a significant factor in the imminent U.S. midterm elections.

sources.title: Binance says 90% of $6.3 billion hack losses are now covered, plans to resume withdrawals Sunday
sources.text:
Binance said Saturday that it has covered up to 90% of the roughly $6.3 billion in token assets stolen from its hot wallets in a record crypto theft announced Thursday.
Binance said it will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets through market and over-the-counter channels until the covered amount reaches 100% for all tokens.
"All BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC are fully backed 100%," Binance said in a statement. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users."
The exchange said the outstanding 10% consists of tokens outside its top 10 that are "less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts."
Binance said it is tapping its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a portion of its Futures insurance fund, and its corporate treasury to replenish the assets.
"Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident. We will continue to demonstrate this commitment through measurable progress, transparent reporting, and concrete actions," Binance said.
Its "next milestone" will be resuming withdrawal services for users by Sunday, subject to security checks, while the exchange continues its investigation into the attack, it said.
Binance declined to discuss additional details or updates on its investigation to CNBC, referring questions to its latest statement.
It still isn't clear how the attack — the largest crypto theft on record — took place.
The world's largest crypto exchange initially said the hack may involve "a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." However, Co-CEO Richard Teng later said the attack involved a more complex process rather than the misuse of a single engineer's permissions.
It also wasn't clear who was responsible for the breach. But TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and AI investigations company, pointed to North Korean hackers as the potential culprits.
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst," the company said.
— CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report.

sources.title: ملخص الأسبوع | مضاعفة باقة الإنترنت الأساسية و iPad mini OLED والمزيد
sources.text:
ملخص الأسبوع | مضاعفة باقة الإنترنت الأساسية و iPad mini OLED والمزيد
شهدت الأيام الماضية موجة متنوعة من الأخبار التقنية، حمل بعضها تغييرات تمس المستخدم مباشرة، بينما فتح بعضها الآخر الباب أمام تطورات أكبر في الذكاء الاصطناعي والهاردوير والألعاب. جاءت أبرز المفاجآت محليًا مع مضاعفة سعة باقة الإنترنت الأرضي الأساسية في مصر دون زيادة السعر، في حين كشفت آبل عن أول iPad mini بشاشة OLED، وعادت Half-Life 3 إلى دائرة الشائعات مرة أخرى.
امتدت الأخبار كذلك إلى تحركات جديدة من OpenAI، واستثمارات ضخمة من SpaceX في عتاد NVIDIA، وارتفاع أسعار بعض بطاقات RTX، إلى جانب أخبار بارزة تخص AMD. إليكم أبرز ما لفت الأنظار من أحداث خلال هذا الأسبوع.
مصر تضاعف باقة الإنترنت الأساسية
حصل مستخدمو الإنترنت الأرضي في مصر على تغيير لافت هذا الأسبوع، بعد توجيه شركات الإنترنت الثابت لمضاعفة سعة الباقة الأساسية من 50 إلى 100 جيجابايت شهريًا دون زيادة قيمة الاشتراك. يظل السعر عند 150 جنيهًا قبل الضريبة، أو 171 جنيهًا شامل ضريبة القيمة المضافة، بينما لا يغير القرار سرعة الاتصال نفسها أو أسعار الباقات الأعلى. تأتي الخطوة بعد طرح باقة 50 جيجابايت بالسعر نفسه في مايو الماضي، وتمنح مستخدمي الفئة الأساسية ضعف كمية البيانات الشهرية دون تحمل تكلفة إضافية.
أول iPad mini بشاشة OLED
كشفت آبل عن جيل جديد من iPad mini يحصل للمرة الأولى على شاشة OLED قياس 8.5 بوصة، إلى جانب معالج A20 Pro المصنوع بدقة 2 نانومتر ودعم أوسع لتشغيل مهام الذكاء الاصطناعي محليًا. أصبح الجهاز أنحف مع حواف شاشة أقل سماكة، كما حصل على مقاومة الماء والغبار بمعيار IP67 ودعم Wi-Fi 7 و Bluetooth 6. يبدأ السعر من 699 دولارًا لنسخة Wi-Fi، على أن تبدأ الطلبات المسبقة في 28 أكتوبر ويتوفر الجهاز تجاريًا في 6 نوفمبر داخل مجموعة من الأسواق العالمية.
شكاوى مبكرة من iPhone Duo
لم تمر الأيام الأولى بعد إطلاق iPhone Duo القابل للطي بهدوء، إذ ظهرت شكاوى من عدد محدود من المستخدمين حول تلف الشاشة الداخلية أثناء الاستخدام المعتاد. وصفت الحالات المتداولة شعورًا بمقاومة غير طبيعية أثناء فتح الهاتف، يعقبها صوت فرقعة ثم ظهور خطوط وتلف في الشاشة الداخلية، ما وضع المفصلة ضمن الاحتمالات المطروحة لسبب المشكلة.
عرضت آبل استبدال بعض الوحدات المتضررة، لكن نطاق الخلل وسببه الحقيقي لم يُحسما حتى الآن، لذلك لا يمكن الجزم بوجود مشكلة تصميمية عامة في الجهاز.
OpenAI تعزل نماذجها عن الإنترنت
استأنفت OpenAI تدريب نماذجها المتقدمة والاستدلال الداخلي عليها بعد تشديد إجراءات الحماية داخل بيئات التدريب، مع فصل هذه البيئات عن الاتصال المباشر بالإنترنت.
جاء القرار بعد واقعة حدثت خلال سبتمبر الماضي استطاع خلالها نموذج بحثي الوصول بصورة محدودة إلى الشبكة نتيجة خطأ في الإعدادات. تعتمد الشركة الآن عند الحاجة إلى محتوى الويب على نسخة مخزنة ومحددة مسبقًا بدلًا من منح النماذج اتصالًا حيًا بالشبكة، في خطوة تعكس التحديات الأمنية التي تظهر كلما أصبحت النماذج أكثر قدرة على تنفيذ الإجراءات والتعامل مع الأدوات الخارجية.
وكلاء Claude اخترعوا ألعابهم
كشفت تجربة بحثية لافتة عما يمكن أن يحدث عندما يُترك وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي لاستكشاف بيئة رقمية دون تكليفهم بمهمة محددة. وضع الباحثون 13 وكيلًا يعتمدون على Claude Opus 4.7 داخل جزيرة افتراضية لمدة وصلت إلى 30 ساعة لكل وكيل، فبدأوا في ابتكار تحديات وأنشطة بأنفسهم، مثل بناء الأبراج واستخدام عناصر البيئة لإنشاء ألعاب جديدة.
المثير أن الخبرات التي اكتسبها الوكلاء أثناء هذا الاستكشاف ظهرت لاحقًا في قدرتهم على حل مهام أخرى، ما يدعم فكرة استخدام اللعب والاستكشاف المفتوح كوسيلة محتملة لتطوير قدرات الوكلاء.
SpaceX تطلب آلاف معالجات NVIDIA
تستعد SpaceX لتصبح واحدة من أكبر المشترين لأنظمة NVIDIA المخصصة للذكاء الاصطناعي خلال عام 2027، وفق تقديرات تشير إلى حصول الشركة على نحو 20 ألف وحدة من أنظمة Vera Rubin NVL72، رغم طلبها المبدئي الذي وصل إلى 30 ألف وحدة.
تمثل الكمية المتوقعة نحو 21% من إجمالي الأنظمة المقدرة للسوق خلال العام المقبل، في ظل توسع SpaceX في البنية التحتية للحوسبة والذكاء الاصطناعي. يأتي ذلك بالتزامن مع استثمارات مالية ضخمة، إذ تحدث إيلون ماسك عن جمع الشركة عشرات المليارات من الدولارات من الديون لتمويل مشترياتها من عتاد NVIDIA.
أسعار بطاقات RTX تواصل الارتفاع
شهدت أسعار بطاقات GeForce RTX 5080 و RTX 5070 Ti ارتفاعات جديدة في السوق الصينية وسط استمرار أزمة الذاكرة. وصلت الزيادة في بعض طرازات RTX 5080 إلى ما يعادل 300 دولار تقريبًا، بينما ارتفعت بعض نسخ RTX 5070 Ti بنحو 100 دولار.
تتزامن هذه التحركات مع تقارير عن استعداد NVIDIA لإطلاق نسخة جديدة من RTX 5080 بسعة ذاكرة 24 جيجابايت وبسعر أعلى، ما يزيد الضغوط على سوق البطاقات الرسومية الذي لا يزال يتأثر بمحدودية المعروض وارتفاع تكلفة مكونات الذاكرة.
AMD تقدم هديتها الأخيرة لـ AM4
كشفت AMD عن الخلفية وراء إعادة طرح معالج Ryzen 7 5800X3D، إذ جاء القرار بمبادرة من الرئيسة التنفيذية Lisa Su لتقديم ترقية أخيرة لمستخدمي منصة AM4 بعد نحو عقد كامل من الاعتماد عليها. اضطرت الشركة إلى إعادة تجهيز عمليات التصنيع لإنتاج إصدار جديد من المعالج، الذي أصبح منذ ظهوره عام 2022 أحد أبرز خيارات الألعاب على المنصة بفضل تقنية 3D V-Cache.
أكدت AMD أن القرار سبق أزمة ذاكرة DDR5 الحالية، وأن الهدف الأساسي كان منح أصحاب أجهزة AM4 فرصة ترقية قوية دون الانتقال إلى لوحة أم وذاكرة جديدتين.
Half-Life 3 تعود للشائعات
عادت Half-Life 3 إلى الواجهة بعد ظهور الاسم الرمزي HLX خلال حديث لمصمم الموسيقى Mike Morasky في مؤتمر GameSoundCon. كان موراسكي يتحدث عن استخدام تقنية HDR Audio داخل مشروعات Valve المختلفة، قبل أن يذكر Deadlock و HLX، وهو الاسم الذي ربطه متابعون منذ فترة بمشروع ج

sources.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
sources.text:
- Published
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist.
The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider.
Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit.
The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds.
America's lead federal agency for investigating financial crimes added that it would "identify the cyber criminals responsible and bring them to justice", while Binance also said it was working with the FBI.
While Binance said its US-facing exchange was unaffected, the US would still have jurisdiction to investigate the hack and help track down stolen funds - an effort which generally involves a global law enforcement effort.
The hack also involved some US-linked assets, such as stablecoins Tether and Circle – cryptocurrencies pegged to the dollar.
Binance told its users "your money is safe, and we're covering every loss".
It had initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals - but then said in an update that "deposits remain unaffected".
Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said: "This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach."
Teng also describes how the hackers used "a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate".
Initially, the company had indicated the breach "may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop" but later statements have pointed to a broader breach.
In a later update, the firm said it had "set aside" more than $6.34B in company funds to cover the stolen assets and was "actively buying" a range of crypto tokens.
The Binance hack spooked cryptocurrency markets on Friday. The price of Bitcoin was down 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York.
Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase was down 12% as investors also reacted to earnings results in which the firm reported revenue slightly below expectations. Robinhood, a financial services company that trades in cryptocurrency, was down 7.8%.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
A lot of the fear right now from Binance users - and the crypto industry at large - is whether or not Binance will actually be capable of covering this enormous financial loss.
The company has said repeatedly that customer funds will be covered and that the firm is strong enough to weather the storm.
But crypto history watchers have been pointing out online that this is exactly the kind of message that FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried gave before his crypto exchange collapsed in 2022, leading to huge losses for customers and the industry.
Several experts have warned customers not to regard Binance's promise to cover losses as legally binding and said they may need to pursue litigation to recover them.
Daniel Tunkel, of the London-based Edwin Coe law firm, said that would "come down to what [customers] have been promised in their contracts", and "where Binance can be sued for non-performance, if it comes to it".
Binance has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
Meanwhile, AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said that several elements of the attack resembled earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
In the last five years the crypto industry has been beset by enormous losses from hackers.
In nearly all cases investigators have blamed hackers from North Korea, pointing to the infamous Lazarus Group - also know as TraderTraitor. The names refer to clusters of cyber criminals accused of working directly for the regime.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, said it had "high confidence" that a North Korean is linked to the hack.
North Korea is an impoverished country with very little industry and heavy international sanctions and experts say the regime uses cyber crime as a way to bring money in.
North Korea has always denied this, but the wealth of evidence from cryptocurrency flow analysis and insider interviews from defectors is compelling.
It makes North Korea likely to be the only nation that uses hacking as a way to raise public funds.

sources.title: Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack
sources.text:
- Published
Two major blockchain analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprits in the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
The Lazarus Group, a North Korean hacking unit also known as TraderTraitor, was identified "with high confidence" by TRM Labs, as well as Chainalysis.
This incident is just the latest linked to the country, one of the poorest in the world and where access to the internet is severely restricted.
Experts accuse the government of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un of relying on cybercrime to finance itself, something Pyongyang has long denied.
Though not financial, the nation's most spectacular suspected hack took place in 2014. The target: Sony Pictures, which had made the Hollywood film The Interview. The film involves a plot to assassinate Kim.
The resulting hack exposed thousands of embarrassing emails exchanged among the studio's top executives.
Last year, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said North Korea was responsible for the theft of $1.5bn on the Bybit exchange.
In the aftermath of that incident, the agency said TraderTraitor had moved to quickly launder and disperse the stolen assets, converting them to Bitcoin and other digital assets with a goal of eventually turning them into hard currency.
The FBI has broadly accused North Korea of "illicit cybercrime and virtual asset theft activities".
The nation has systematically developed its cyber operations, recruiting the most promising students from universities and channeling them into hacker groups overseen by North Korea's intelligence agency, according to reports.
Some of the cyberwarfare conducted takes place just over the nation's border in China, according to analysis from tech groups.
Much of its hacking activity has centred on monetary gain.
North Korean hackers are also suspected in the theft of $620m worth of cryptocurrency in 2022.
In this most recent heist, North Korean agents are accused of using a special authorisation to turn a Binance hot wallet, which is connected to the internet, into one that moved funds automatically to the attacker.
TRM said it's likely the attacker gained access to Binance's hot wallet signing system as part of the scheme.
Binance has not directly responded to the BBC's queries about the incident's potential links to the area.
The company had initially said it thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider.
"Our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," Binance's co-CEO Richard Teng said.
Some 80% of stolen assets have been secured, a Binance spokesperson said on Friday, but the rest remains unaccounted for.
If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become – a sign that the tools of the hacking trade have grown sharper.
Experts say the rise of artificial intelligence has also given threat actors new ways to carry out crime, through automation and other means.
In this case, it's plausible that AI was used to infiltrate Binance's systems.
As Chainalysis put it, the attacker used laundering patterns "we have not seen before".

sources.text:
Hackers working for the North Korean regime have been blamed for a record cryptocurrency heist following a cyberattack at crypto exchange Binance. The hackers stole at least $6.3 billion in crypto from the company’s wallets, though about half of that amount was frozen as the stolen crypto traveled across various blockchains, according to security researchers.
The breach is by far the largest known theft of crypto in history, though the incident has not been confirmed yet to be resolved, and the amount of crypto stolen may change.
In a post on X, Binance said its initial investigation showed that the hackers broke into the company’s network after targeting a “compromised” Binance engineer’s laptop, which “allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
Binance said it has seen no evidence of a leak of its private keys, which would grant the hacker near-unfettered control over the company’s stores of crypto.
The crypto exchange — the world’s largest — said it has now suspended all deposits and withdrawals while its investigation into the breach continues. TechCrunch reported on Thursday that the exchange had paused withdrawals across some of its blockchains.
Binance said “user funds are safe,” but did not immediately provide proof of this claim. The company said it will “publish an updated proof of reserves once the remediation is complete.”
Spokesperson Andie Cooper said in a statement shared with TechCrunch on Friday that some $3 billion has been frozen by industry partners. The spokesperson said Binance has “begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.”
It’s unclear how the hack went down or under what circumstances the employee’s laptop was compromised, but it’s not uncommon for security incidents to stem from the use of compromised software on employee devices.
Software is generally built from many components, including open source projects, which hackers regularly target, compromise and modify in order to steal data from devices that the affected software is installed on. Other times, malware bundled with regular-looking apps and games can allow hackers to steal usernames, passwords, and session tokens from infected computers, which may let them log in as if they were a legitimate employee.
Binance will face questions about why the company’s security allowed a single employee’s laptop to access systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in funds.
Spokespeople for Binance did not respond to an email with questions about the breach. TechCrunch has also asked the company who, if anyone, performed a security audit of Binance’s network and systems prior to the hack. Companies regularly ask third-party companies to stress-test their security to identify weaknesses that could be exploited by attackers, but it’s unclear if Binance sought such a review.
Security researchers at TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and forensic company, attributed the breach to North Korean hackers, and called it the “largest hack in history.”
Researchers describe the network of hackers, known in the cybersecurity industry as TraderTraitor, as a North Korean cell focused almost exclusively on stealing crypto from large companies and exchanges. This group was also blamed for the now-second-largest heist on record, a $1.4 billion theft from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.
According to TRM, the theft of Binance’s billions in crypto took about 20 minutes.
Blockchain security firm Elliptic also attributed the Binance theft to North Korean hackers. Elliptic said some of the stolen funds ended up in the same wallet that was used in a previous cyberattack on crypto exchange Bitget earlier this year, in which hackers stole $351 million.
The U.S. government and its allies have long warned about the threat from North Korea, which remains cut off from the U.S. and the global financial system for its ongoing development of its nuclear weapons program. Researchers say the breakaway country’s sole motivations are to steal as much crypto as possible in order to continue developing its sanctioned weapons of mass destruction.

clusters.title_hint: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust

sources.title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
sources.text:
Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger. Until now, only two genuinely ancient Martian meteorites were known: Allan Hills 84001, found in Antarctica, and a jumbled rock from northwest Africa nicknamed Black Beauty. Now we have a third one.
A team led by Yang Liu, a planetary scientist at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, has shown that a Martian meteorite called Teghaza 001, found in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. “It's very old and similar to some of the oldest rocks on Earth,” Liu says.
“We don't fully understand why old Martian rocks are so rare on Earth," Liu said. Part of the answer may lie in how a piece of Mars gets here. It takes a large impact to launch a rock off the planet, and not every rock can survive that. “If the impact hits into loose powder, it may not get cemented to become a rock and fly off Mars' gravity,” Liu said. “So the natural impact already acts as a filter. Weak rocks do not make it off Mars.”

sources.title: Reddit stock plunges 29% after weak outlook, wrapping its worst day ever
sources.text:
Shares of Reddit cratered 29.22% on Friday, the worst drop since becoming a public company in 2024, after the company forecast weak fourth-quarter sales in its latest earnings report.
The previous record low was set on July 31, when the stock dropped 20.99%.
The social media company on Thursday projected fourth-quarter sales between $1 billion and $1.03 billion, below analysts' estimates of $1.05 billion. Reddit reported Q3 sales growth of 53% over a year ago, weaker than previous quarters, but beat Wall Street expectations on both earnings and revenue.
The report comes as the company has seen a shift in its search referral traffic with the rise of Google's AI Overview. In an interview with CNBC, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to AI.
Reddit announced on Thursday that it plans to test requiring users to log in to access content, a dramatic change from a site whose community-based discussion content has become synonymous with the open internet. Google's shift towards pushing AI overviews in search results coincided with the change, intended to help boost the number of logged-in users that are more active on the platform, which in turn helps the company's advertising business, according to Huffman.
"Reddit is the last platform to provide basically unfettered logged-out access, and that's largely because of me. I've been holding that line," Huffman said. "I think users will probably go through the same understanding that I have, which is that it's a sign of the times. It's an evolution of how these platforms work."
Multiple analysts downgraded the stock following Reddit's disappointing results, with Citizens noting that "search changes highlight the problem with selling content to Google" and that as referral problems worsen, uncertainty around user growth amid the login requirement switch "puts more pressure on user monetization."
— CNBC's Jonathan Vanian contributed to this report.

clusters.title_hint: A Supply Chain Attack Put Malicious Anthropic Claude Extensions on Thousands of Devices

sources.title: A Supply Chain Attack Put Malicious Anthropic Claude Extensions on Thousands of Devices
sources.text:
The AI software-development platform Cursor, which is owned by SpaceX, had a malicious Anthropic Claude Code extension for Windows, macOS, and Linux live in its integrated development environment extension marketplace for roughly 11 hours on Thursday. The company says the rogue extension was downloaded by “at most 5,000 users.” Cursor briefly shut down the extension marketplace while it investigated the situation, which the company says did not impact any other extensions.
The tainted extension was designed with a backdoor to give attackers access to victim devices—the type of implant that malicious hackers often use as a stepping stone to deeper control inside a target network. Cursor published remediation steps on Thursday for the roughly 5,000 affected targets. A saving grace of the situation, though, was a flaw in the malware's design that blocked it from fully establishing itself on the vast majority of targets.
“Everyone was so lucky here, this was potentially a really dangerous foothold for an attacker,” says Calum Hall, cofounder and CEO of the detection firm Phorion, the first researchers to spot the malicious extension after detecting it on a customer's Mac.
What is still unclear is how the malicious extension made its way into the Cursor marketplace at all. Some researchers initially speculated that it came from a compromised Anthropic system. But Cursor said in its Thursday security alert that “these malicious versions of the extension were not developed by Anthropic.”
Felix Rieseberg, a member of Anthropic's technical staff, posted on X on Friday: “We’re working with Cursor on this incident, but it wasn’t a compromise of Anthropic’s systems or employee laptops. A malicious actor used access to Cursor’s marketplace to publish a tampered copy of the Claude Code extension, which we didn’t build or publish. The versions on our official channels are not affected and this only impacts Cursor users.”
David Dworken, who works on security at Anthropic, posted on X shortly after, explaining that “this did not involve a compromise of any Anthropic systems … We were not involved with building, publishing, or hosting this.”
Cursor did not return WIRED's request for comment about how the malicious upload happened and whether it was the result of a breach at Cursor.

clusters.title_hint: Judge Again Tosses Out Donald Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit Against The Wall Street Journal Over Its Reporting On Jeffrey Epstein Birthday Letter

sources.title: Judge Again Tosses Out Donald Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit Against The Wall Street Journal Over Its Reporting On Jeffrey Epstein Birthday Letter
sources.text:
A federal judge has again dismissed Donald Trump‘s $10 billion defamation lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal over its reporting on a letter sent to Jeffrey Epstein for his birthday in 2003.
U.S. District Judge Darrin P. Gayles wrote in his opinion that Trump’s lawsuit “falls short of pleading actual malice. Indeed, the allegations regarding malice are conclusory, vague, sometimes inconsistent with the Article, and often irrelevant to whether Defendants knew or should have known that the statements in the Article were purportedly false.”
Trump sued the Journal as well as a series of other defendants, including Rupert Murdoch, after it published an article in 2025 reporting on the contents of a bawdy letter bearing Trump’s name and included in a “birthday book” compiled for Epstein’s 50th birthday.
In its story, the Journal reported that the letter “contains several lines of typewritten text framed by the outline of a naked woman, which appears to be hand-drawn with a heavy marker,” adding that a “pair of small arcs denotes the woman’s breasts, and the future president’s signature is a squiggly ‘Donald’ below her waist, mimicking pubic hair.”
Watch on Deadline
Trump has claimed that he did not compose the letter. The article did include Trump’s denial that he composed the letter, and that he was preparing to sue. Also named in the lawsuit were parent Dow Jones, News Corp. CEO Robert Thomson and reporters Khadeeja Safdar and Joseph Palazzo.
The judge previously tossed out Trump’s case, concluding that it failed to allege actual malice, but allowed it to be amended. The judge’s latest ruling, though, is with prejudice, meaning the same claim cannot be refiled.
Trump intends to appeal the ruling.
A spokesman for the president’s legal team said the president “will continue to press forward in his powerhouse lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and all of the other defendants. The President will continue to hold those who mislead the American People with Fake News and smears accountable for their actions.”
In his opinion, the judge opened with a quote from Justice Louis Brandeis in his concurring opinion in New York Times vs. Sullivan, the landmark 1964 Supreme Court ruling that set the precedent for public figures seeking defamation claims. It set the standard that public figures had to prove actual malice, or that a media outlet published a story with knowledge that it was false or that it was done with reckless disregard for the truth.
Brandeis wrote, “Those who won our independence believed … that public discussion is a political duty; and that this should be a fundamental principle of the American government.”
More to come.

sources.title: Trump loses legal battle over Epstein-linked Wall Street Journal case
sources.text:
A federal judge has permanently dismissed United States President Donald Trump’s multibillion-dollar defamation lawsuit against media mogul Rupert Murdoch and The Wall Street Journal.
On Saturday, US District Judge Darrin Gayles concluded that the president had failed to establish the standard of “actual malice” required for defamation suits.
Recommended Stories

- list 2 of 3Trump administration subpoenas New York Times reporters over coverage
- list 3 of 3US judge dismisses Trump’s $10bn lawsuit against WSJ over Epstein story
Under US law, a successful complaint must show that the defendant released a defamatory statement knowing it was false or with “reckless disregard” for its accuracy.
Gayles, however, said that Trump was “grasping at straws” with his $10bn case against The Wall Street Journal.
“The Amended Complaint falls short of pleading actual malice,” Gayles wrote.
“Indeed, the allegations regarding malice are conclusory, vague, sometimes inconsistent with the Article and often irrelevant to whether Defendants knew or should have known that the statements in the Article were purportedly false.”
The judge went so far as to suggest that Trump’s legal team had attempted “to manufacture flaws with the investigation” published in The Wall Street Journal.
The case stemmed from coverage that linked Trump to the late disgraced financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
On July 17, 2025, The Wall Street Journal published an exclusive describing a sexually suggestive birthday note gifted to Epstein for his 50th birthday in 2003, as part of a book of congratulatory letters.
The letters were reportedly collected by disgraced British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell, who is serving a 20-year prison sentence for her involvement in Epstein’s sex-trafficking scheme.
The note attributed to Trump includes typed text framed by a hand-drawn outline of what appears to be a curvaceous woman. At the bottom, where her pelvic region might be, is Trump’s signature.
Trump vehemently denied responsibility for the text, the signature and the artwork. A copy of the birthday letter was later released through the House Oversight Committee.
The Wall Street Journal’s article came at a time when Trump’s second administration was facing intense scrutiny over whether it had withheld documents about Epstein’s alleged sex crimes, despite promises of transparency.
Critics had also raised questions about the nature of Trump and Epstein’s relationship. The two men appear to have socialised together, and Epstein was known to have surrounded himself with powerful figures from politics, academia and the business world.
In 2025, Trump said he ended his relationship with Epstein after the financier “stole” female employees from his Mar-a-Lago resort.
Epstein was convicted of soliciting a minor for sex in Florida in 2008, for which he served 13 months in jail. In 2019, he faced federal charges related to sex trafficking, but he was found dead in his New York City jail cell before he could be brought to trial. His death was later ruled a suicide.
Legal advocates say Epstein’s victims are estimated to number in the hundreds.
After the release of The Wall Street Journal report, Trump branded the newspaper’s coverage “false, malicious, and defamatory”.
His lawsuit, filed in the federal court in Miami on July 18, 2025, accused the paper and its reporters of having “knowingly and recklessly” published “numerous false, defamatory, and disparaging statements”.
The result, it alleged, was “overwhelming financial and reputational harm” to the president. Two journalists associated with The Wall Street Journal article were named among the defendants.
In April, Judge Gayles dismissed the defamation lawsuit, ruling that Trump had failed to prove the reporting was borne of “actual malice”.
But that initial ruling gave Trump the opportunity to refile his complaint, which he did in May.
The updated lawsuit claimed The Wall Street Journal had been reckless in not showing how reporters had received and verified the letter.
Saturday’s Miami ruling deals a final blow to Trump’s attempt to sue over the issue. Gayles’s decision dismisses the case “with prejudice”, which effectively blocks any future litigation on the matter.
Trump has other ongoing defamation cases against other media outlets, including the BBC and The New York Times.

clusters.title_hint: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals

sources.title: Things That Go Beep in the Night: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
sources.text:
While science fiction lore tells us that humans will meet extraterrestrial life in the form of little green men, the detail that should raise hairs this Halloween is this: the search for extraterrestrial intelligence took a major leap forward with AI, and it increasingly focuses on AI agents built by humans listening for AI agents built by aliens.
Some scientists have suggested that extraterrestrial civilizations, if they exist, could be billions of years older than humanity. Such civilizations might have developed technologies far beyond humanity’s, including forms of AI.
Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute are bringing agentic AI into the daily search for extraterrestrial intelligence. At the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California, agents can now steer the instrument, enhance and correct incoming data, and apply AI models to the incoming stream — all from a single natural language request. The NVIDIA Holoscan platform processes the massive streams of sensor data, giving agents live data to act on.
The result is a faster, more adaptable search for potential signals from extraterrestrial life and technologies.
“As our new agentic observatories reach out into the universe, what they find may have much more in common with themselves than with the humans who created them,” said Andrew Siemion, Bernard M. Oliver chair for SETI at the SETI Institute and principal investigator of Breakthrough Listen. “But this isn’t something to fear. Rather, it’s a breakthrough in translation.”
Radio telescopes generate enormous volumes of data, creating a challenge for scientists who need to identify potentially interesting signals as observations unfold.
At the Allen Telescope Array, DAQIRI, a Holoscan platform library, enables the telescope to pull terabits per second of sensor data straight into GPU memory so observations are processed in flight rather than filling hard drives. CyberEther, a signal-processing framework developed at the SETI Institute, does the math using NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries including cuFFT and cuBLAS.
Nexus, a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness. It gives agents a single source of truth for instrument state, compute resources and pipelines and lets researchers monitor packet loss, read live spectrograms and rewrite signal-processing blocks — all by prompting in natural language. The system can handle 2.4 terabits per second on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference running on premises, next to the instrument.
Put together, the system enables an agent to steer a telescope’s antennae, calibrate and focus the instrument for a clean signal, catch and fix data errors and plot the result. Agents compress what would take humans weeks or years into hours.
The pipeline has already proven itself, achieving the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar — a rapidly spinning stellar remnant that pulses like a cosmic lighthouse — in the Crab Nebula.
Next, the team is evaluating open models including NVIDIA Nemotron for cases where data locality and turnaround matter most and for observatories that may someday run offline on the far side of the moon.

sources.title: Analysts find looming launch crisis is "more severe" than anticipated
sources.text:
A new report from the analytics firm Quilty Space confirms that, outside of China, the world faces a significant shortage of rockets over the next five years.
The firm estimates that between now and 2030, there will be a shortfall of about 150 launches compared to demand from satellite operators and civil space agencies. If demand from the US military is added in—and SpaceX does not extend the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy program to accommodate increased national security needs—the shortage could be doubled.
"What we wanted to get at is to understand how severe this launch crisis is and when will it be resolved," said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space. "What we learned is that the launch crisis is more severe than we thought and that it will not go away this decade for sure, and it might not abate until sometime late in the 2030s."

sources.text:
India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30).
A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time).
Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff.
NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System (GPS).
NavIC operates on a smaller scale than its American counterpart, however. It's "a regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) service to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km [930 miles] beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area," ISRO officials wrote in the NVS-03 launch brochure.
The Indian constellation currently consists of three fully functioning satellites, and it requires four to provide PNT services. So today's launch was a big deal — and a lot of eyes will be watching NVS-03's commissioning and checkout phase.
Today's launch was the 14th to date for the GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) Mark II, a three-stage rocket that stands 170 feet (52 meters) tall. Twelve of those 14 liftoffs have been successful.
The GSLV Mark II debuted in 2010, the same year its predecessor retired. That previous launchers, the Mark I, flew a total of six times, with two failures.
NVS-03 was the fourth Indian launch of 2026 and the third operated by ISRO. The fourth was mounted by Skyroot Aerospace, which in July became the first Indian company ever to successfully reach orbit.

sources.text:
“I think I’m going to switch back to my other iPhone.”
I’ll admit, I said this multiple times during my five-day vacation with the new iPhone Duo, after encountering frustrations with broken apps, unfamiliar gestures (a return to Touch ID, argh!), and camera concerns that had me lugging around two phones.
By the time the trip was over, I didn’t want to go back.
When I first unboxed the Duo, a loaner from Apple, I was genuinely intrigued. I felt a flutter of anticipation as I peeled back the factory seal wrap and booted up the device. In retrospect, this was probably the first signal that Duo was going to ultimately win me over.
As a tech reporter, I’ve received a lot of test devices over the years, so unfortunately, opening a package with a new gadget inside is no longer the thrill it used to be. But sometime in the days leading up to the Duo’s ship date, I found myself actually wanting one – I had started doing the math and comparing upgrade options that would allow me to afford the $2K the phone would cost. I started scrolling TikTok reviews of Duo cases. I hesitated not only because of the price but because moving to the Duo is a major change – especially coming from an iPhone 17 Pro Max. The phones could not be more different.
As I was about to head out on vacation when the Duo arrived, I decided to tote my 17 Pro Max with me too, as something of a safety net. I ended up using the Duo more, and grew comfortable with it over the course of the trip, despite some frustrations.

sources.text:
كشف تقرير حديث من شركة استخبارات بلوكتشين أمريكية أن وحدة قرصنة تابعة لكوريا الشمالية تقف على الأرجح وراء الاختراق الضخم لمنصة Binance، الذي تجاوزت خسائره 6.3 مليار دولار، في أكبر حادثة من نوعها تسجل في قطاع العملات الرقمية.
وأوضحت Binance أنها تمكنت، بالتعاون مع شركاء في مجال البلوكتشين، من تجميد نحو 3 مليارات دولار من الأصول المتأثرة بالهجوم، وبدأت الجمعة باستعادة بعض الأصول للعملاء.
وأكدت الشركة أن عمليات الإيداع لم تتأثر، في حين لا تزال عمليات السحب معلقة بشكل مؤقت ويتوقع استئنافها خلال يوم أو يومين، مع التزام المنصة بتغطية جميع الخسائر الناتجة عن الاختراق.
وقالت Binance عبر X إن التحقيقات الأولية أشارت إلى أن جهاز لابتوب مخترق ربما استخدم في الهجوم، إلا أن التحقيقات اللاحقة كشفت عن نقاط اختراق إضافية.
شركة TRM لتحليل البلوكتشين أرجعت الهجوم إلى مجموعة “TraderTraitor”، والتي وصفتها بأنها وحدة نخبة في عمليات الاختراق تابعة لكوريا الشمالية.
وأفاد تقرير TRM أن المهاجمين نقلوا نحو 6.36 مليار دولار من محافظ Binance على عشر شبكات بلوكتشين خلال حوالي 20 دقيقة، وهو ما جعل العملية الأكبر في تاريخ السرقات الرقمية.
وأشارت TRM إلى أن العديد من السمات التقنية لهذا الهجوم تتطابق مع هجمات سابقة منسوبة لكوريا الشمالية، وبينها الاختراق الذي تعرضت له منصة Bybit في فبراير العام الماضي بقيمة 1.5 مليار دولار.
أكدت شركة Chainalysis المتخصصة في تحليل البلوكتشين، أن الهجوم يعود على الأرجح لمجموعة TraderTraitor أيضاً، بحسب ما صرح به المؤسس والمدير التنفيذي جوناثان ليفن.
رفض متحدث باسم Binance تقديم تفاصيل حول الاشتباه في ضلوع كوريا الشمالية، لكنه شدد على أن الشركة تعمل بشكل وثيق مع جهات إنفاذ القانون لتحديد هوية المهاجمين ومحاسبتهم.
ويرى محللون أن كوريا الشمالية زادت من أنشطتها في مجال القرصنة الرقمية سعياً لجمع العملة الصعبة لاقتصادها المتعثر، وتمويل برامجها النووية وسط العقوبات الدولية.

من جانب آخر، أوضح تشانغبينغ زاو، مؤسس Binance، أن أموال المستخدمين آمنة، رغم إقراره بأن الحادثة “تبدو كاختراق مباشر للمنصة”. وأكد أنه يتوقع تغطية جميع الخسائر حتى بعد تركه لمنصب الرئيس التنفيذي للشركة.
أثار الحادث أيضاً انتقادات حول سبب ضعف ضوابط الوصول والمصادقة في Binance، خاصةً بعدما أشار كووك تين جان، المؤسس والرئيس التنفيذي لشركة NyxLab للأمن السيبراني، إلى أن الهجوم اعتمد على توقيع وحيد منح المهاجم تصريح وصول كامل إلى محفظة Binance ساخنة لأجل غير محدود.
في المقابل، قالت Binance إنها لم تجد أي دليل على تسرب مفاتيح المحافظ الرقمية، مؤكدة عزمها نشر تفاصيل فنية شاملة بعد اكتمال تحقيقها.

sources.title: The reason most electrical plug prongs have holes in them
sources.text:
The reason most electrical plug prongs have holes in them
Those little holes play more of a role in making the plug than they do in your home’s wall outlets
Of all the things in the world to sit back and contemplate, holes in electrical plug prongs are one of those great mysteries. It's right up there with the hollow moon theory and underground military bases in Antarctica. Not really. The truth is, while these enigmatic holes once served an everyday purpose (more on that below), they are mainly useful in the manufacturing process today. They help manufacturers position the metal blades during manufacturing, but they aren't openings for electrical current or portals to another dimension.
Basically, a worker passes an alignment rod through the holes to hold the blades in position before plastic is molded around the assembly. The holes also serve as lockout tags, a necessary safety mechanism. A once sensible purpose in the home is now a holding, positioning and locking convenience for manufacturers. It's a simple way to keep components correctly aligned during production. That goes for ordinary plugs on a vacuum cleaner to smart plugs for smart home integration (just don't plug a power strip into your smart plug).
Of course, not every manufacturer uses the same process. It does answer the "why" of today's perforated plug prongs (say that three times really fast!), a feature that doesn't need to perform a specific job in your outlet, but is still useful in a factory.
The outlet-gripping explanation has a history
You've probably come across the "holes help an outlet grip the plug" explanation. It's a sensible answer that's no longer grounded in reality. According to the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA), the holes originally worked with a small raised feature inside the receptacle. That feature basically clicked into the hole to help retain the plug. The mechanism is known as a "detent."
Detents still have uses outside of ordinary household electrical plugs, but that deserves its own, separate article. Later, Underwriters Laboratories (UL) revised the standards on receptacles to hold plugs in place without the holes. Those requirements also limited how difficult a plug can be to remove, with a different test gauge that didn't have holes. Most manufacturers stopped adding the matching raised features because they did nothing to help meet minimum requirements and made the plugs more difficult to withdraw.
The detent design in wall outlets went away accordingly, but the holes in plug blades did not, leaving the design feature entirely optional, with most manufacturers continuing to use them. Outlets are now designed to hold the blades in place, and the holes are still compatible with older receptacles. It works either way, whether your household receptacles are ancient or just installed yesterday.
Can I use a plug without holes?
You sure can. A plug without any holes isn't defective or anything, and it's not missing the required safety features, though some plugs, like extension cords, shouldn't be plugged in at all times for safety. If a manufacturer produces a plug with holes, it has to follow the specified size and lead-in shape to maintain compatibility with old and new receptacles. The burden is on the manufacturer, not the buyer.
A solid, hole-free blade will still make electrical contact and close the circuit in an appropriate outlet (including those with retractable prongs). Older receptacles use the detent, and newer receptacles must meet the minimum requirements for plugs without holes. Either way, you're good to go.
The only practical concern you have to worry about is the condition of the connection. If your plug is sliding back out with little resistance, it's probably wear and tear in the receptacle, not the plug prongs. You don't need to go out and hunt for a plug with holes. Instead, go find a new receptacle. Changing them out isn't too difficult; just make sure the power is cut off at the breaker. Fingertips and 15 to 20 amps don't mix well. Also, don't drill holes in the prongs if you have a plug with solid blades. The holes really aren't necessary.

sources.text:
The Wikimedia Foundation weighs in on the NYT's case against OpenAI
The folks behind Wikipedia say that an extreme decision in either direction could threaten the open web.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
The Wikimedia Foundation has weighed in on the copyright lawsuit launched by The New York Times against OpenAI and Microsoft. The people behind Wikipedia have filed an amicus brief urging nuance in the case, which seeks to decide whether or not OpenAI and Microsoft's use of content published in The New York Times for any purpose, including AI model training, is a violation of copyright law.
The New York Times says that companies like OpenAI shouldn't be given free reign over any of their published content. OpenAI and Microsoft say that training and deploying AI models based on published data is necessary for technological development and would therefore fall within the definition of fair use.
The Wikimedia Foundation, however, is seeking a third way. The amicus brief agrees with Microsoft and OpenAI and suggests that a much more restrictive version of fair use could inhibit tech innovation. However, it also says that a ruling in favor of blanket fair use could lead to a closed web where knowledge is weakened due to a "lack of available secondary source materials."
The platform's alternative position applies fair use to two specific use cases for AI companies. This includes certain model training scenarios and something called retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). This is a technique that optimizes the output of large language models (LLMs) by referencing authoritative knowledge bases outside of its training data. However, the organization does not support RAG if an LLM is regurgitating pre-existing articles without attribution.
As for the specifics of model training, the Wikimedia Foundation argues that scraping copyrighted content should be considered fair use if it's being used when "training LLMs that are something new and different from the original sources." It is worth noting that Wikipedia itself is considered one of the highest-quality datasets used to train LLMs.
"A ruling that does not apply fair use principles carefully could threaten the sustainability of free knowledge, and stifle the development of open source technologies, ultimately impacting access to information for everyone in both cases," the Wikimedia Foundation's General Counsel Stephen LaPorte wrote. "The court needs to understand that Wikipedia is created through a collaborative process that requires a strong foundation of open and accessible human knowledge to thrive."
A summary judgment in the lawsuit is expected in the near future. This is just one of over a dozen similar cases working their way through the courts, but it could set an important precedent.

Akai teased its new MPC Sample Key on Instagram earlier this week, and said it plans to open-source its software so the modding community can hack it to their hearts’ delight. While there’s no word yet on when the device will launch or how much it will cost, The Verge has received exclusive images of the upcoming instrument that offer some details about its feature set.
Exclusive details about Akai’s MPC Sample Key
The open-source MPC Sample Key won’t be focused on chopping up drum breaks.
The open-source MPC Sample Key won’t be focused on chopping up drum breaks.
While the Sample Key shares many of the same controls as the MPC Sample — including the three context-sensitive encoders, a large main encoder — it seems designed for pitched sample playback, rather than chopping up drums. In fact, the “chop” button from the MPC Sample is missing entirely from the Sample Key.
The dedicated pitch and mod wheels are another clue there. But there are also buttons for changing the octave range of the 25-key keyboard, as well as ones labeled “chord” and “arp.” Presumably, those enable a chord playback mode and an arpeggiator. While using an arpeggiator to play back drum samples can be a fun way to create rhythms, it’s more commonly used for melodic and bass parts. And a chord mode would be basically useless for drums. Those options also appear to replace the chop function from the standard MPC Sample.
There also appears to be a dedicated looper that could be useful for live performance and layering sounds. And, instead of the Flex Beat effects from the original MPC Sample, there’s something called “Swarm.” Though what that is isn’t exactly clear at the moment.
Like the first entry in the Sample series, the Key has a built-in mic and speaker for all-in-one music production. While we haven’t gotten a glimpse at the back panel yet, the config options on the front suggest that, in addition to MIDI, the Sample Key will have CV outs for integrating with modular synths.

sources.text:
More than a decade after the Sony hack shook Hollywood, Martin Scorsese is still reeling from the fallout of the North Korean state-sponsored digital attack.
The Oscar-winning director recalled how the wide-reaching hack, which was a response to Seth Rogen‘s 2014 film The Interview, “ruined everything” for Scorsese’s planned Cleopatra feature, which would have starred Angelina Jolie.
“Remember we were gonna do Cleopatra at one point, and then they made fun of [Kim Jong Un], and he got mad and he blew up everybody at Columbia,” he told daughter Francesca Scorsese on Tribeca’s Crafty. “Seth Rogen, right? And then he got mad, and [it] ruined Cleopatra.”
Martin added, “We were gonna do it. We were ready on the script. Angelina Jolie—We were going. She was gonna be Cleopatra VII. It was gonna be really wild.”
Watch on Deadline
As Francesca told her father she’s “so mad about” the fate of the film, Martin quipped, “Well, tell Seth, because they ruined everything. Just because Kim Jong Un doesn’t have a sense of humor.”
In The Interview, co-written and directed by Rogen and Evan Goldberg, celebrity tabloid show host Dave Skylark (James Franco) and his producer Aaron Rapaport (Rogen) land a rare interview with Kim Jong Un (Randall Park). When the CIA catches wind, they enlist the pair to assassinated the North Korean dictator.
Despite the unintended consequences of The Interview, Scorsese and Rogen have moved on, as the former even played himself in last year’s debut episode of the latter’s Apple TV series The Studio. Since Rogen’s studio head character Matt Remick ends up responsible for Scorsese’s passion project getting axed, could the storyline be another meta example of life imitating art in the smash show?

sources.title: Martin Scorsese Says His ‘Cleopatra’ Movie With Angelina Jolie Was ‘Ruined’ by Seth Rogen and the Sony Hack: ‘It Was Gonna Be Really Wild’
sources.text:
Martin Scorsese‘s “Cleopatra” never came to fruition, and he says the Angelina Jolie-starrer was nixed because of Seth Rogen and the Sony hack.
For those who need a refresher, Sony emails were hacked in November 2014 by a group that hoped the Seth Rogen comedy “The Interview,” which was about a fictional assassination attempt of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, would not be released by Sony.
According to Scorsese, this caused some aftereffects in the industry, which he described in the first episode of the Tribeca original series “Crafty.”
“We were gonna do Cleopatra at one point, and then they made fun of [Kim Jong Un], and he got mad and blew up everybody at Columbia,” Scorsese said. “Seth Rogen, right? And then he got mad, and [it] ruined Cleopatra.”
Though Rogen wasn’t directly responsible for the project being canceled, the resulting hack exposed thousands of emails, including ones from producer Scott Rudin to Sony’s Amy Pascal calling Jolie “a minimally talented spoiled brat.”
“We were gonna do it,” Scorsese also said. “Angelina Jolie. We were going. She was gonna be Cleopatra VII. It was gonna be really wild.”
The film was set to be written by screenwriter Eric Roth, who wrote Scorsese’s 2023 film “Killers of the Flower Moon.”

If any of these messages sound familiar, it’s likely because they’re part of the massive stream of text messages flooding your phone leading up to the US midterm elections on Tuesday. The scale of the issue is not entirely clear, but call-blocking company Robokiller found that 15 billion political texts were sent in 2022, thanks in part to a Supreme Court decision the year prior that made it easier to send some mass calls and texts without consent. Alex Quilici, CEO of spam protection service YouMail, has an even higher estimate of 25 billion to 30 billion political texts this year, but caveats it’s an informal approximation. The volume is about the same to 10 percent higher than in 2024, he says.
There’s some good news and some bad news about these messages, says PIRG consumer watchdog director Teresa Murray. “The bad news is that political calls and political texts are exempt from the do-not-call-list rules,” Murray says. “The good news is that the election is next Tuesday, and hopefully within a few days after that, we’ll know what the results are and there won’t be any need to have any texts, or calls, or emails anymore after that.”
There are still some things consumers can try to stem the flow of these messages blowing up their phones — but it likely won’t significantly reduce it before Tuesday.
“In between all of the ‘legitimate’ political texts … there are going to be some scams in there”
The simplest thing you can do is send “stop” or block and report the messages as spam, which will notify your service provider of a likely spam number. That probably won’t result in any immediate change, Murray says, but if enough people report the same number in a certain period of time, the provider might begin to block it or label it as spam. You can also file a complaint with the Federal Communications Commission or your state attorney general if you believe a number is using an autodialer without your consent — something that even the people behind political texts are not supposed to do. Whatever you do, Murray says, do not click any links you receive from numbers you don’t know.
“In between all of the ‘legitimate’ political texts that are going out to support this candidate, or vote against that candidate, or vote for this issue, or whatever, there are going to be some scams in there,” Murray says. “If you want to donate money at this point, I would recommend going directly to the website for that political candidate, or for that PAC, and donating it that way.”

sources.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
sources.text:
The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know.
Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky.
Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer.
Stargazers in Australia, Indonesia and a host of other island nations and territories will see the moon pass directly in front of Jupiter, hiding its light in an event known as an occultation starting at 3:45 p.m. EST (2045 GMT) on Nov. 2 , according to In-The-Sky.org. However, the exact visibility and timings depend on location.
The cosmic pile-up serves as a spectacular reminder of the scale and diversity of targets on display in the night sky. After all, the moon appears largest from our Earthly perspective, but in reality it's less than half the diameter of Mars.
Jupiter, meanwhile, is over 20 times wider than the red planet, while mighty Regulus is up to four times larger than the sun, andcould easily fit all the planets of the solar system in its vast expanse.
By moonrise on the night of Nov. 3, the lunar crescent will have leapt past Jupiter and Mars, to appear just 1 degree from the blue-white light of Regulus for viewers in the U.S. Meanwhile, viewers in several South American countries including Brazil, Peru, Argentina and Bolivia will see the moon occult Regulus beginning at 6:59 EST (1024 GMT) on Nov. 3. clusters.title_hint: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'

sources.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
sources.text:
On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier.
During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon. So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.
NASA called the asteroid the "Great Pumpkin," while others called it the "Halloween Asteroid."
Why it mattered
Be afraid, be very afraid... Okay, not really, but there is reason to be concerned about near-Earth objects and the time in which they are detected.
"According to the catalog of near-Earth objects (NEOs) kept by the Minor Planet Center, this is the closest currently known approach by an object this large until asteroid 1999 AN10, at about 2,600 feet (800 meters) in size, approaches at about 1 lunar distance (238,000 miles from Earth) in August 2027," NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) reported in 2015.
NASA’s Near-Earth Object Observations Program, sometimes called “Spaceguard,” works to catalog these type of objects and predicts some of their paths if they could be potentially threats to our planet. While there are no known credible impact threats to date, it doesn't mean the "Great Pumpkin," or rather a great impactor, isn't real.
As for 2015 TB145, it did return to Earth's vicinity in 2018, but at a much more distant pass of about 24 million miles (38 million kilometers), "or about a quarter the distance between Earth and the sun," according to JPL.

sources.title: NASA's second year-long Mars simulation mission ends today
sources.text:
NASA's second year-long Mars simulation mission ends today
The agency will livestream the event starting at 3PM Eastern time.
The second set of volunteers for the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) mission is exiting NASA's mock Mars habitat after 378 days. NASA will stream the event live on YouTube and on its social media accounts, starting today at 3PM Eastern time. Ross Elder, Matthew Montgomery, Ellen Ellis and James Spicer entered the habitat on October 19, 2025, as part of the CHAPEA mission 2 crew.
They lived inside a 3D-printed 1,700-square-foot facility on NASA Johnson grounds in Houston, Texas for over a year, conducting Mars mission operations right here on Earth. They did simulated spacewalks, performed habitat maintenance and grew plants. The crew even has to go through an airlock to leave the habitat. In addition to the isolation, the participants were subjected to other stressors future spacefarers to Mars and the moon would face, like communication delays and resource limitations.
NASA started looking for volunteers for the CHAPEA missions in 2023, and the first crew entered the habitat in June that year. The agency has already started accepting applications for the Moon and Mars Exploration Analog for another year-long experience that combines elements of CHAPEA with NASA's other space simulation experiences. That mission will begin no earlier than August 2027. NASA says data from the missions can help it optimize food system design for its future lunar missions and prepare for the other aspects of spending long stretches of time in space.

sources.title: Northflank security breach leads to abuse of customers' AI API keys
sources.text:
Cloud application hosting platform Northflank is warning customers to rotate all credentials and secrets stored on its platform after a security breach led to unauthorized use of customers' AI API keys.
Northflank is a cloud platform that allows developers to deploy and manage applications, containers, databases, and AI applications without managing the underlying infrastructure.
The company disclosed a security incident on October 30, warning customers to immediately rotate their environment variables and API keys after receiving a threat alert from cloud security company Wiz.
Soon after, Northflank told all customers to assume their environment variables had been decrypted and that the secrets stored within them were stolen.
"Assume all environment variables have been decrypted. Disable/rotate all keys," Northflank warned in an October 30 update.
Applications commonly use environment variables to store sensitive information, including database passwords, cloud service credentials, authentication tokens, and API keys.
If exposed, these credentials can be used to breach other customer services, potentially leading to data theft or unauthorized charges through API keys.
Northflank later confirmed that multiple customers had reported unauthorized use of AI API keys stored on the platform.
"Users have reported unauthorised use of AI API keys supplied to the Northflank platform," the company said.
"If you have not already rotated your user-provided secrets stored in Northflank, please do so immediately."
Customers were also advised to review their AI provider usage and billing logs for unexpected activity and report suspicious usage to Northflank and their AI providers.
According to Northflank's published incident timeline, Wiz warned them about the breach at 11:43 UTC on October 30, which the company's engineers reviewed one minute later.
Northflank quickly responded with a network policy patch, followed by additional patches at 12:50 UTC and 13:05 UTC. The company also requested assistance from Wiz's incident response team.
The company has not disclosed how attackers gained access to its systems, how many customers were affected, or whether attackers stole or abused credentials other than the reported AI API keys.
As part of its response, Northflank enabled credential rotation for PostgreSQL, MongoDB, MySQL, and Redis.
The company also enabled audit logs for all customers, including those using free accounts, to help them investigate any suspicious activity.
Northflank continues to advise customers to rotate secrets stored in workloads, secret groups, and global secrets, and to disable public access to add-ons where enabled.
BleepingComputer contacted Northflank with questions about the breach, its impact on customers, and whether stored credentials were accessed or stolen, but has not received a response.
Black October
The breach comes amid a series of attacks targeting AI development platforms, which security researchers believe are valuable targets because they store API keys that can be used to access expensive AI services.
In a report titled "Black October for AI Developer Platforms," Wiz identified at least nine security incidents affecting AI development platforms during the month, including Northflank, Railway, OpenCode, Warp, and Lightning AI.
The Railway incident also involved potential exposure of decrypted customer environment variables, while OpenCode disclosed exposed AI API keys. Warp reported a breach that exposed AI agent logs and user telemetry data.
Wiz says attackers involved in some of these incidents have specifically targeted environment variables containing AI service credentials, which can be exploited through a practice known as LLMJacking.
LLMJacking involves using stolen credentials to access AI models using another organization's API keys, generating massive API charges or allowing the stolen access to be resold.
In two cases investigated by Wiz, compromised enterprise credentials were used to make approximately 2.5 million Amazon Bedrock API calls, generating approximately $100,000 in AI usage.
The researchers also discovered infrastructure linked to services reselling access to AI models, although they could not link those operations to the initial breaches or large-scale abuse.
Wiz has not confirmed that all nine incidents were conducted by the same attackers. However, many of the incidents involved attempts to steal AI API keys.
Northflank also referenced Wiz's research in its incident updates, noting that customer reports of unauthorized AI key usage may be tied to the attacks seen by the researchers.

sources.text:
الصحراء الغربية: الجزائر تأسف لعدم تجديد ولاية البعثة الأممية والمغرب يرحب
أعربت الجزائر السبت عن أسفها تجاه عدم تجديد ولاية بعثة الأمم المتحدة في الصحراء الغربية، وانتقدت ما اعتبرته "بالانحياز المفرط" لصالح لرباط، فيما رحب المغرب بذلك، قائلا إنه ينبغي لأفراد البعثة المغادرة في الأيام المقبلة. وكانت روسيا استخدمت الجمعة حق النقض ضد مشروع قرار صاغته الولايات المتحدة بشأن مستقبل المنطقة. وبررت موسكو اعتراضها على المشروع الأمريكي بأنه "تمادى في تأييد الموقف المغربي" بحسبها.
عبرت وزارة الشؤون الخارجية الجزائرية السبت عن أسفها إزاء عدم تجديد ولاية بعثة الأمم المتحدة في الصحراء الغربية، منتقدة ما وصفته "بالانحياز المفرط" لصالح المغرب في مشروع القرار الذي صاغته الولايات المتحدة.
ووجه سيدي محمد عمار، ممثل جبهة البوليساريو، الشكر لروسيا على استخدام حق النقض ضد مشروع القرار الأمريكي والذي قال إن من شأنه "أن ينسف أسس عملية السلام التي تقودها الأمم المتحدة" و"يهدد السلام الإقليمي والدولي".
وعلى الجانب المغربي، رحب الديوان الملكي بعدم تجديد مهمة البعثة، قائلا إنه ينبغي لأفرادها المغادرة وأن تخرج معداتها من الصحراء الغربية في الأيام المقبلة. وأكد المغرب أنه لا يزال ملتزما بوقف إطلاق النار.
اقرأ أيضاالصحراء الغربية: فيتو روسي وآخر أمريكي يحولان دون تجديد ولاية بعثة الأمم المتحدة
النقض الروسي
واستخدمت روسيا حق النقض ضد قرار صاغته الولايات المتحدة بشأن الصحراء الغربية في مجلس الأمن أمس الجمعة، مما عرقل تجديد التفويض لبعثة حفظ السلام التابعة للأمم المتحدة هناك قبل يوم واحد فقط من انتهائه.
وقالت روسيا إن مشروع القرار الأمريكي "تمادى في تأييد موقف المغرب" من الإقليم المتنازع عليه. وقال مبعوث روسيا لدى الأمم المتحدة فاسيلي نيبينزيا "نشدد على حقيقة أن مجلس الأمن لا يمكنه أن يحسم استباقيا مسائل تتعلق بالسيادة". وأضاف "يجب ألا يمنح مجلس الأمن مباركة لمثل هذا النهج أحادي الجانب، ولذلك اضطررنا إلى منع اعتماد مشروع القرار".
وكان من شأن هذا القرار تمديد مهمة البعثة لعام آخر مع ترسيخ خطة المغرب للحكم الذاتي أساسا وحيدا للمحادثات الرامية إلى تسوية الصراع المستمر منذ نصف قرن، وتقليص مكونها العسكري.
مواجهة تهدد مستقبل البعثة
ورفض مجلس الأمن مشروع قرار روسي منافس يقترح تمديد البعثة لعام. وحصل على ثلاثة أصوات مؤيدة وصوت واحد معارض، مع امتناع 11 عضوا عن التصويت، مما حال دون نيله الأصوات التسعة المؤيدة اللازمة لتمريره. وكان هذا القرار سيديم وجود البعثة في المنطقة بصيغتها المعروفة.
وتهدد هذه المواجهة غير المعتادة مستقبل بعثة دأب المجلس على تجديد التفويض لها لعقود، وتوسع الخلاف بشأن الإقليم الذي يسيطر المغرب على معظمه، بينما تطالب به جبهة البوليساريو، المدعومة من الجزائر، التي تسعى إلى إقامة دولة مستقلة.
وإذا لم يتفق مجلس الأمن على تمديد المهمة في اللحظات الأخيرة، ينتهي السبت تفويض بعثة الأمم المتحدة للاستفتاء في الصحراء الغربية، المعروفة باسم مينورسو.

The District of Columbia (DC) and the state of Virginia have filed a joint lawsuit to halt the construction of a large triumphal arch sought by United States President Donald Trump.
Filed on Saturday, the lawsuit denounces the project as “flagrantly unlawful” and “legally indefensible”.
